breaking_changes.BC_description: Direct internal imports (e.g., importing from 'redux/lib/createStore') are no longer supported because Redux now bundles CommonJS and ES modules. This change ensures that internal module reorganization does not affect external consumers, but it breaks any code relying on private module paths.

Calling getState, subscribe, or unsubscribe during dispatch (such as inside a reducer) now throws an error. Previously, this was allowed but could lead to inconsistent state or unpredictable behavior.
The ActionTypes constant (e.g., @@redux/INIT) has been moved to a private export and is no longer part of the public API. Direct usage of ActionTypes in user code may break.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Avoid relying on ActionTypes constants directly. If needed for debugging or special cases, access them only through the official Redux public API or consider alternative patterns. There is no direct replacement for importing ActionTypes.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The legacy 'jsnext:main' field in package.json has been removed. Tools or bundlers that relied on this field to resolve ES modules may fail to resolve Redux modules correctly.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Ensure your build tools use the standard 'module' or 'exports' field to resolve ES modules. Most modern bundlers (e.g., Rollup, Webpack 4+) already prefer 'module' over 'jsnext:main'. No code change required, but verify tooling compatibility.
